datasets.name: ArabSign
datasets.version_or_subset: RGB modality of the full release: 50 sentences by 6 signers, at least 30 takes per sentence per signer, 9,330 mp4 files verified in the six archives. Entry paths encode signer/split/sentenceID/signer_sentence_(timestamp)_c.mp4, so sample labels come from the path. The target paper runs MediaPipe pose over these colour frames rather than using the Kinect skeleton modality, which is a different estimator (25 joints in 3D camera space versus MediaPipe's 33 landmarks in 2D).
datasets.license_or_permission: The dataset is publicly available from direct Drive links on the author's project page; what is missing is licence information, not access. No licence is published anywhere for ArabSign. A search on 2026-09-18 found no licence, terms, copyright, permission, consent, ethics, or IRB statement in the dataset paper (arXiv:2210.03951, full text); no LICENSE, COPYING, TERMS, or agreement file among the 60 paths of github.com/Hamzah-Luqman/ArabSign (GitHub API reports "license": null); and no terms on the official project page or on the same author's KArSL page. The archives carry only a citation request in Readme.txt. The "NC only" value in the REPRO-SIGN dataset record is that record's own characterisation, not a published term. The operative basis is therefore the dataset author's direct permission: the assignee contacted Hamzah Luqman (KFUPM), who supplied the official download page https://hamzah-luqman.github.io/ArabSign/ for REPRO-SIGN project use, reported on 2026-09-18. Earlier, the author had provided Team S with the copy transferred on 2026-09-10 that supplied Skeleton and partial Depth. The RGB archives this reproduction added on 2026-09-18 came from the public download links on that same author-published page. The assignee authorised study use and project-cloud processing on that basis. The copy stays private to the repro-sign Modal workspace, no video or frame is redistributed or published, and the requested citation is recorded in reproduction.json.sources.

experiments.system: Task: closed-set classification of a whole sentence video into one of 50 fixed classes. This is neither isolated sign recognition, which labels individual signs, nor continuous recognition, which outputs gloss sequences; the model never segments and never produces language, so Table III is not comparable with either literature or with ArabSign's own WER benchmark. Proposed temporal-to-spatial residual CNN. MediaPipe pose keypoints for 10 frames per video, 33 landmarks with x and y, giving input shape (10, 33, 2); Conv2D with 32 filters; three residual blocks (32; 64 stride 2; 128 stride 2); flatten; Dense 128; Dense 50. 755,346 parameters. Adam, categorical cross-entropy, batch size 32, 100 epochs; learning rate 0.001 is not stated in the target paper and is carried from reference [19], which §IV says supplied the same training parameters.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: None published. The paper describes a fixed 100-epoch run and reports final-model metrics; no best-checkpoint selection or early stopping is mentioned, and Figure 3(a) shows testing loss rising slightly after about 40 epochs without any action taken.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table III, ResNet column; architecture in §III and Table I; training settings and hardware in §IV.

gates.reason:
The two papers describe the 10-frame input differently and neither states which frames are taken. The target paper §III says "Each input sample consists of 10 consecutive frames" without saying where the window starts. Reference [19], which §IV says supplied the same setup, instead says it converts "the input video into a sequence of ten frames", which reads as sampling across the whole clip. ArabSign clips run 1.3 to 10.4 seconds at 30 fps, so the readings present materially different inputs: ten consecutive frames cover about 0.33 seconds of an average 4.3-second sentence. [19] lists the framing approach as future work, so neither paper resolves it.

Both alternatives were implemented and run before either was selected, with the decision rule recorded first. Uniform sampling reproduces 0.9886 accuracy against the published 0.9777; the literal consecutive reading reproduces 0.7230. The assignee selected uniform-10-across-clip on 2026-09-21 as the working reading, on [19]'s text and on the inference that a protocol which cannot produce the published numbers is not the one the authors used. That selection governs which runs are reported, but it does not resolve the published ambiguity: the 25-point spread shows the choice is behaviour-changing, so both runs are conditional evidence and no target is marked produced.
evidence: Target paper §III: "Each input sample consists of 10 consecutive frames, where each frame contains 33 keypoints with x and y coordinates, resulting in an input shape of (10, 33, 2)."
Reference [19] §4: "The mission of the first stage is to convert the input video into a sequence of ten frames"; "we retain 10x66 numpy vectors corresponding to ten frames per video".
Reference [19] §6 lists the open question: "it would be interesting to precisely evaluate the impact of the framing approach on the subsequent stages."
Target paper §IV: "We adopted the same training parameters as our previous work[19]", which is why [19]'s description is treated as evidence about this paper's setup.
ArabSign paper Table II: minimum video duration 1.3 s, maximum 10.4 s, 30 fps, average 130.3 frames per sentence.
Neither paper states a window position, a stride, or a sampling rule.
gates.required_action: Only the authors can state which ten frames Table III used. Until then the requested numbers cannot be reproduced faithfully, and the conditional runs stand as evidence of what each reading yields. Author contact on this point is available now that an independent attempt is complete.

alternatives.description: Frames 0 through 9 of each clip, contiguous, with MediaPipe temporal tracking enabled because the frames are adjacent.
alternatives.paper_evidence: Follows the target paper's explicit word "consecutive" in §III. The window position is not stated; frame 0 is chosen as the simplest deterministic reading, matching the first-N precedent in papers/ahmad-2022-intelligent-landmarks.
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept that the target paper's own wording governs, and that the unstated window position is a documented choice.

alternatives.description: Ten indices spaced evenly from the first to the last frame of each clip, with MediaPipe temporal tracking disabled because the frames are not adjacent.
alternatives.paper_evidence: Follows reference [19]'s description of converting a whole video into ten frames, which §IV of the target paper says supplied its setup. Contradicts the target paper's word "consecutive".
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept that [19]'s description governs where the target paper's wording conflicts with the prior work it says it inherited.
